newsitem.title: UK: London freight market seen lacking direction.
newsitem.headline: London freight market seen lacking direction.

text.p: The London dry cargo freight market saw difficult trading conditions for Panamaxes and Handy-sizes, brokers reported on Tuesday.

In a market that some described as "shapeless" and "lacking direction", early Panamax tonnage struggled to find even steady rates in the US Gulf while the Pacific market saw a few particularly weak fixtures.
The Baltic Freight Index lost eight points to end at 1,424.
Some brokers expect more enquiry from grain charterers for December Panamaxes and Handy-sizes to emerge in the near future.
Fresh enquiry for Capers on Tuesday and a reported shortage of vessels available for December fixture boded well for Caper rates, market sources said.
GRAIN - Business in the main US Gulf trades was thin.
South Korean charterers Seyang was said to have fixed 52-54,000 tonnes heavy grain for the US Gulf to Japan for December 5-15 with Hanjin tonnage at $23.50 no combo and then failed on subjects.
Dreyfus was reported to have booked for 55,000 tonnes heavy grain US Gulf-Kosichang for November-December at a firm $22.50.
Barley fixtures to Saudi Arabia dominated grain business on Tuesday.

Dreyfus took two Panamaxes and Toepfer took one from the Canadian Pacific for first-half December at between $20.12-1/2 and $20.75, and Glencore fixed a prompt 30,000-tonne parcel from Newcastle to Jeddah at a shade under $24.00, brokers said.
Andre were linked with a fixture of 50,000/10 tonnes heavy grain Nopac-South Korea for mid-December at $14.65 (possibly Seorax).
Some brokers were predicting a build-up of early Panamaxes like Oinoussian Sky 64,453 dwt and Derby North 64,491 dwt at the South West Pass.
But others vessels in prompt positions, such as Ioannis P 64,100 dwt, Fortune 65,716 dwt and Kordun 72,050 dwt were said to have been fixed already (Kordun to Docenave on private terms).

New grain orders included Continental with 25,000 tonnes corn Lakes-St Lawrence/Gdynia-Gdansk for December 3-9, Azure 25,000/10 tonnes agri-products Plate/Holland-Belgium for mid December onwards and Shipmair 1.4-1.8m cubic ft delivery Paranagua-Santos range for a trip Gibraltar-Skaw range December 15-25.
Cargill put in a fresh enquiry to cover 55,000/5 tonnes wheat Port Kembla/Egyptian Med for December 10-17.
MINERALS - There were few Caper fixtures but a number of fresh enquiries, traders said.
China Steel was in the market for January coal tonnage for eastern Australia/Kaohsiung coal and 120,000 tonnes iron ore Brazil/Kaohsiung, they said.
Some brokers said Caper tonnage may be in short supply in December.
In the Panamax trades, K Line was said to have booked tonnage from Brazil to the East on private terms.

Vessel owners described as disappointing the reported fixtures of the 1994-built Hanjin Tacoma 70,457 dwt to HMM delivery prompt Ulsan for a trip via Queensland with coal to Hong Kong at $12,000 daily, and the 1984-built Alpheos 62,635 dwt delivery Nopac for an early December trip to the Far East at $10,000 daily plus $175,000 bonus.

HANDY-SIZES - LD-Seals was said to be actively chartering craned tonnage on the Continent for trips to the Far East and Italmare and was reported to have taken a 38,000 dwt vessel delivery Canakkale for a trip via the Black Sea to Karachi, details unavailable.

Olympic Mentor 29,000 dwt was reported booked on subjects from the US Gulf to the Far East, possibly by Pan Ocean while Aghia Sophia 43,000 dwt was said fixed from Goa to Japan and Feyza 47,00 dwt by Finagrain for short period business, both on private terms.
